370309.title: Asymptotic scarcity of Legendre cordial labelings for complete graphs

gates.source: Actual 2509.09528v1 acquired; definition, Lemma 3.1 proof through Claim 7 start, Corollary 3.4, the criterion algorithm and Conjecture 3.5 read. Theorem 3.3 was seen only through its proof end, Corollary 3.4 and the algorithm lines 36-37.
gates.ordinary: Author-complete proof, explicit and stronger than the limit. On K_n every bijection gives the same edge counts. Let chi be the Legendre character with chi(0)=0 and n=qp+r, 0<=r<p, n_a=q+eps_a. e(1)-e(0)=Q-Z with Q=sum_{x<y}chi(x+y), Z=#{x<y: p|x+y}. Orthogonality kills every q-term: sum_{x,y}chi(x+y)=sum eps_a eps_b chi(a+b) and sum_x chi(2x)=sum eps_a chi(2a), so |Q|<=(p^2+p)/2. Z>=q^2(p-1)/2+q(q-1)/2. For q>=p+1, i.e. n>=p(p+1), Z-|Q|>=2, so K_n is not Legendre cordial mod p. Hence J(n,m)=0 for all n>=m(m+1).
